entities.summary: Kiribati is a sovereign nation in Micronesia, Oceania. Its capital is South Tarawa. Official languages include Gilbertese (Taetae ni Kiribati), English. Government: Unitary presidential republic. Population: approximately 0.1 million. Area: 811 km². Comprehensive index for Kiribati covering Micronesian settlement (~2000 BCE), Austronesian seafaring, European contact (Spanish/British 16th-18th century), Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony (British 1892-1979), WWII (Battle of Tarawa 1943, bloodiest US Marine landing), phosphate mining (Banaba/Ocean Island devastation), independence 1979, nuclear testing (Christmas Island/Kiritimati British H-bomb tests 1957-62), climate change existential threat (lowest-lying nation, 2m average elevation, relocation planning).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kiribati's vulnerability to climate change and its efforts to relocate its population pose a significant global concern, with the nation's very existence threatened by rising sea levels. The country's history of nuclear testing and phosphate mining also have regional implications.
